title: Duty roster synthesis and incident handback protocol
author: Leah Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document standardizes how we build duty rosters (rotas), synthesize overlapping coverage windows, and perform incident handbacks between responders. The goal is to reduce knowledge loss during shift transitions, ensure timely customer communication, and preserve investigational evidence for post-incident analysis.

Scope: Applies to all on-call engineers, SREs, and incident bridge operators responsible for Redwood Inference production services (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane). Does not replace service-specific runbooks — it augments them with handoff and roster-level rules.

Intended audience: on-call engineers, incident leads, SRE managers, customer-success on-call liaisons.

Key definitions
- Shift: a contiguous on-call assignment (typical length 8 or 12 hours).
- Handback window: the 20-minute overlap period reserved for warm transfer between outgoing and incoming responders.
- Evidence package: structured set of logs, traces, and artifacts captured for postmortem and regulatory evidence.
- Bridge Operator: primary coordinator for the incident bridge and external comms.

Principles
- Prioritize clarity: every handoff must include a short status summary, current mitigation state, and next action list (top 3).
- Make evidence immutable: when feasible snapshot traces and logs before changing system state.
- Prefer short, consistent templates for customer comms and status page updates.
- Automate where possible: roster publishes to Slack, calendar invites include handback reminders, handoff checklist persisted to incident ticket.

Duty roster synthesis (how we design rotas)
1) Shift cadence and lengths
   - Default: 12-hour shifts for primary responders; 8-hour shifts permitted for trainees and cross-team coverage.
   - Night coverage: when region has full-coverage teams, prefer 12-hour with 24-hour overlap on rotation change days (major releases).
2) Predictable overlaps
   - Reserve 20 minutes overlap at each shift boundary as a handback window. This is mandatory and cannot be used for pager swaps.
   - For critical services (SLO: 99.95% availability), add an additional 10-minute escalation buffer during high-traffic windows.
3) Shadow and backup assignments
   - Each primary shift has an assigned shadow (buddy) for the first two weeks after onboarding. Shadow shifts are half-duration and scheduled mid-shift for knowledge sharing.
4) Roster artifacts and automation
   - Roster publishes as a CSV and auto-posts to #oncall-status daily at 06:00 UTC.
   - Calendar invites include: shift owner, shadow, on-call playbook link, pager escalation matrix, and handback checklist link.

Handback protocol (step-by-step)
Pre-handback: (Outgoing)
1) Prepare your evidence package:
   - Snapshot the incident ticket with current timeline (timestamps ISO 8601).
   - Attach top-5 relevant logs (service, ingress, egress, kgv-cache stats, scheduler events) limited to 30MB total.
   - Export a 15-minute trace span surrounding the root-causing request (if available).
2) Draft the 3-line status summary (SMS format):
   - Line 1: Current impact and customer-facing symptom.
   - Line 2: Active mitigations and owners of each mitigation.
   - Line 3: Immediate next actions and risk level (low/medium/high).
3) Notify: post the status summary in the incident bridge and mark your calendar for the handback window.

During handback: (Overlap window)
1) Live voice/video: prefer a 5–10 minute live sync in the bridge channel. If voice unavailable, use the bridge chat and a short Loom or transcript.
2) Walkthrough agenda (5 bullets):
   - One-sentence incident summary.
   - Evidence artifacts and where to find them.
   - Active mitigations and their health checks.
   - Outstanding actions (owner and ETA).
   - Escalation triggers (explicit threshold values) and next-level contacts.
3) Incoming confirms: the incoming responder repeats back the top 3 next actions and acknowledges evidence locations.

Post-handback: (Outgoing)
1) Set the incident ticket field "handoff_complete" to true and add a 1-paragraph handover note.
2) Outgoing stays available for 15 minutes post-handoff for clarifying questions unless otherwise agreed.

Emergency hot-handover (when overlap cannot occur)
- Execute a cold handover: outgoing posts a preformatted incident stub and the evidence package, then immediately notifies the incoming responder via SMS/phone. The incoming responder must acknowledge within 5 minutes or escalate to L2 on-call.

Incident evidence package (required elements)
- Ticket timeline (ordered list of events with UTC timestamps).
- Key metric slices: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, queue depth, GPU utilization (select 1–6 metrics relevant to service). Include pre-incident baseline and current window.
- Traces: root spans + top 3 child spans for the top failing path.
- Config snapshot: model-serving config (model version, quantization profile, batching settings), routing policy, and traffic split.
- Any recent deploy IDs (commit hashes) with timestamps.
- Links to long-term storage (S3/GCS) for large artifacts and a checksum (sha256) in the ticket.

Evidence retention policy for postmortem
- Keep short-term (attached to the incident ticket) for 180 days.
- Move curated artifacts (de-duplicated logs, trimmed traces, and config snapshots) to the postmortem folder in the evidence bucket for 7 years if incident meets "regulatory" criteria (customer SLA breach > 99.9% threshold or enterprise contract clause).

Customer communications templates (use and adapt)
- Immediate acknowledgement (within 15 minutes):
  "We’ve detected elevated error rates affecting the Redwood API in region <region>. Our engineers are investigating; we will provide an update within 60 minutes. Impact: <symptom>."

- Status update (1 hour):
  "Update: Root cause is under investigation; mitigation X has been applied (rate-limiter rollback / routing fallback). Customers may see reduced capacity but successful requests continue for most tenants. Next update at <time> or sooner if status changes."

- Post-incident summary (published with postmortem):
  "Summary: On <date> at <time> UTC, a codepath change caused increased latency and 5xx errors for the Hosted API in <region>. Impacted customers: <summary>. Mitigations: <actions>. Root cause: <concise root cause>. Remediation and follow-ups: <bullet list>."

Status page update snippets
- Short status (for banner): "Investigating: elevated 5xx in <region>."
- Medium status (detail):
  Title: Degraded: API error rate increased in <region>
  Body: We are actively investigating an increase in server errors impacting a subset of requests. Partial mitigations in place; monitoring.

Game day and handoff drills
- Objective: validate warm handoff under pressure and evidence preservation.
- Scenario examples:
  1) KV-cache eviction storm causing transient timeouts.
  2) Autoscaler misconfiguration leading to cold-start surge.
  3) Model-loading contention causing elevated latency on long sequences.
- Game-day schedule (90 min):
  - 00–10 min: pre-brief and objectives
  - 10–30 min: inject incident (simulated alerts)
  - 30–60 min: active mitigation; perform at least one handback across a shift boundary
  - 60–80 min: evidence snapshot and ticket finalization
  - 80–90 min: retro and action assignment
- Scoring: measure handback completeness (did incoming confirm: status, mitigation, evidence location). Pass threshold: 90% of handoffs include complete evidence package.

Runbook example: handoff checklist (pasteable)
- Handoff checklist (must complete before marking handoff_complete):
  * [ ] 3-line status summary posted to bridge
  * [ ] Evidence package uploaded and links present in ticket
  * [ ] Active mitigations and monitoring queries shared
  * [ ] Next 3 actions assigned with ETA
  * [ ] Incoming ack recorded in ticket
  * [ ] Outgoing set availability window (15 minutes)

Escalation matrix (short form)
- Pager L1 (primary responder) — 10 minutes to acknowledge
- Pager L2 (service on-call) — escalate if unresolved after 30 minutes or if SLO breach imminent
- Engineering oncall lead — engage if multiple services are impacted or if mitigation requires deploy rollback
- Customer-success escalation — notify when incident impacts >5% of enterprise customers or SLA credit may be required

SLO triggers and automated actions
- If p99 latency > 3x baseline for 5 minutes: auto-open incident ticket and notify L1 via paging system.
- If error rate > 2% (absolute) for 15 minutes: trigger automatic routing fallback to model-variant B and notify bridge operator.

Handoff quality metrics (tracked monthly)
- Handoff completeness rate (target >= 95%).
- Average handback overlap observed (target >= 18 minutes).
- Evidence capture rate (tickets with full evidence package) target >= 98%.

Operational ownership and review cadence
- Roster owner: SRE Ops (primary) — responsible for publishing and automation.
- Handoff protocol owner: Incident Response guild (rotating steward every quarter).
- Review cadence: quarterly review of handback failures and postmortem evidence quality; annual roster redesign aligned with team growth.

Templates & quick commands
- Incident ticket stub (copy into ticket):
  "Short summary: <one line>
  Impact window: <start time>
  3-line status: <status>
  Evidence locations: <links>
  Next actions: <bullets>"
- Helpful CLI snippets:
  - Export recent logs: 
    rinfctl logs export --service api-gateway --since 30m --out /tmp/api-logs.tar.gz
  - Snapshot tracing window:
    rinfctl trace snapshot --service model-serving --span 00:15 --out /tmp/trace.zip
  - Publish to ticket:
    hub ticket comment --id 1234 --body "Evidence uploaded: s3://evidence/incident-1234/"

Appendix: examples of a strong handback note (templates)
- Example short handback note: "Handoff at 2026-03-02T07:40Z. Impact: elevated 5xx for tokenization service in us-west-2. Mitigation: routing fallback to variant-v2 applied (owner: Marcus). Evidence: s3://evidence/incident-5678/ (sha256: abc...). Next actions: 1) Confirm backpressure drains (Owen, 10m), 2) Validate quantization profile (Marcus, 60m). Outgoing available until 08:00Z."

- Example cold handover (emergency): "Cold handover — outgoing cut at 2026-02-11T23:50Z. Posted full evidence package and invited incoming via SMS. Incoming acknowledged at 2026-02-11T23:54Z and confirmed next actions."
